steps.say: Testicular cancer in childhood is uncommon but unmistakable in pattern. It makes up a tiny slice of all childhood solid tumours, strikes hardest around age two and again at puberty, and usually announces itself as a painless swelling of the scrotum that the parent notices.
steps.tx: **Testicular cancer** (testis malignancy) is under **2** (two) percent of paediatric solid tumours with a **bimodal peak** (twin age spikes) near **2** (two) years and at puberty, usually found as a painless **scrotal mass** (ball swelling). Transscrotal biopsy is avoided in favour of the **inguinal approach** (groin control), the core **biopsy principle** (no scrotal violation). Any firm painless paediatric scrotal mass is cancer until proved otherwise.

steps.say: Sound waves characterise the lump and a body scan hunts spread. Ultrasound defines the mass inside the testis, while computed tomography stages the nodes behind the abdomen and distant organs. A blood-borne tumour markers panel completes the staging. Sound waves separate inside lumps from outside ones, and blood markers are drawn first.
steps.tx: **Ultrasound** (sound-wave scan) characterises the mass while **computed tomography** (body scan) stages retroperitoneal **nodes** (belly glands) and distant spread. **Tumour markers** (blood cancer signals) with imaging complete staging before any cut. Scrotal **ultrasound** (sound-wave scan) separates inside-testis from outside-testis lumps, and tumour markers are drawn before surgery.

steps.say: Two blood tests point to the cell type before surgery. The yolk-sac protein rises with yolk sac tumours, while the pregnancy hormone rises with embryonic and mixed tumours containing chorionic elements. Marker trends after surgery track cure or relapse. Marker fade after surgery confirms that all tumour is gone.
steps.tx: **Alpha fetoprotein** (yolk-sac protein) from **yolk sac** (primitive sac) marks yolk sac tumours while **beta hCG** (pregnancy hormone) from **embryonal carcinoma** (primitive cancer) and mixed **teratoma** (multi-tissue tumour) marks choriocarcinoma elements. Falling markers confirm complete resection. Marker **half life** (fade rate) checks after surgery confirm complete removal.

steps.say: Almost all childhood testicular cancers spring from germ cells, splitting into seminoma and the non-seminoma family of embryonic, yolk sac, chorionic and teratoma types. A small minority grows from the hormone-making support cells instead.
steps.tx: Over **95** (ninety five) percent are **germ cell tumours** (sperm-line cancers) split into **seminoma** (uniform germ cancer) and nonseminoma **embryonal** (primitive), **yolk sac** (sac-like), **choriocarcinoma** (placental-like) and **teratoma** (mixed-tissue), while under **5** (five) percent are Sertoli or **Leydig stromal tumours** (support-cell cancers).

steps.say: The specimen shows why the operation must come through the groin. Cut in half, the tumour is a variegated mix of solid grey nodules, small fluid cysts, cartilage flecks and blood. Scrotal violation would seed these layers; the cord is clamped high first.
steps.tx: Gross **orchidectomy specimen** (removed testis) cut in half reveals a heterogeneous variegated tumour with solid grey **nodules** (tumour lumps), small fluid filled **cysts** (sacs), **cartilage** (gristle flecks) and focal **haemorrhage** (bleeding). **Radical inguinal orchiectomy** (groin-route removal) with high cord control is the operation.

vis.alt: Gross orchidectomy specimen cut in half revealing heterogeneous variegated tumour with cysts and nodules.
vis.caption: Variegated tumour with cysts, nodules and haemorrhage in orchidectomy specimen. Credit: The Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP).

steps.say: Spread disease adds drugs and node surgery to the groin operation. Chemotherapy follows the marker-defined type, and a planned clearance of the belly nodes handles residual masses. The six-panel matrix below keeps tumour, torsion, hernia and fluid collections apart at the bedside.
steps.tx: Nodal or metastatic disease adds systemic **chemotherapy** (drug treatment) with modified retroperitoneal **lymphadenectomy** (node dissection) added to radical orchiectomy. The scrotal matrix compares hydrocele, varicocele, hernia, epididymal cyst, **tumour** (hard lump) and **torsion** (twisted cord) by location, transillumination and urgency.

vis.alt: Six scrotal conditions illustrated with comparison table of location and urgency.
vis.caption: Hydrocele, hernia, cyst, tumour and torsion compared for bedside diagnosis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Outlook tracks how far the disease has travelled. Disease confined to the testis cures nearly everyone, regional spread cures most, and distant spread still cures about three quarters of germ cell cases. These are among the best figures in all of childhood cancer.
steps.tx: Five year **survival rate** (cure measure) is **99.2** (ninety nine point two) percent in **localised disease** (confined cancer), **96** (ninety six) percent regional and **73** (seventy three) percent distant for **germ cell** (sperm-line) disease. Stage and marker response, not size alone, drive prognosis and follow up intensity.

steps.say: Support-cell tumours behave differently and deserve their own rule. Early-stage disease still cures four to nine in ten, but once spread the median survival collapses to one or two years. The operation stays the same; the expectations change, requiring honest counselling.
steps.tx: Stage I non germ cell tumours still cure **80** (eighty) to **90** (ninety) percent, but metastatic disease has a median survival of only **1** (one) to **2** (two) years. **Leydig cell tumour** (testosterone-cell cancer) and **Sertoli cell tumour** (nurse-cell cancer) need marker and hormone follow up after inguinal surgery.
